rationale: C02 plausibly supplied the concrete paired-telegram structure used by the child: separate communications from Eisenhower to John F. Kennedy at Hyannis Port and to Lyndon B. Johnson, addressing them in their linked presidential and vice-presidential electoral roles. The child adapts that same recipient pairing and concise telegram format from campaign briefings to post-election congratulations and transition planning. C12 is a plausible generic model for congratulating a president-elect, but it lacks the distinctive Kennedy-Johnson pairing. C20 shares only the brief congratulatory-telegram form.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Senator John F. Kennedy Hyannis Port, Massachusetts ... Senator Lyndon B. Johnson ...
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Honorable John F. Kennedy Hyannisport, Mass. ... the Honorable Lyndon Johnson, your Vice Presidential candidate
shared_material.explanation: Both documents consist of linked communications to the same presidential and vice-presidential candidates, with Kennedy identified at Hyannis Port.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I will be sending you promptly a more comprehensive telegram suggesting certain measures that may commend themselves to you as you prepare to take over next January the responsibilities of the Presidency.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I believe it to be in the national interest ... for you ... to have periodic briefings ... I am offering them to him by telegram today
shared_material.explanation: The earlier paired telegrams establish transition-relevant assistance to both nominees; the later Kennedy telegram continues that administrative function after the election by promising proposed transition measures.
